If the shoulder is a 'restriction' of the SAME saturated closed form, could its envelope be a numerical refinement?
deterministic_restriction_tension_resolv.resolution: NO. 'Deterministic restriction' refers to the DOMAIN of g (the shoulder is the g<143 sub-domain), NOT to the envelope's structural class. The envelope is governed by the per-pole exponent alpha(s) and the Wodzicki degree deg(s), which are pole-keyed (s=5 vs s=4), regulator-invariant, and integer-distinct (grounds 1 + 2). The functional form of the cardinality is ALSO distinct (ground 3: 2^g rising vs C(N,2) flat). A domain restriction does not make the envelope a numerical refinement: the numerical-refinement test asks whether two envelopes have the SAME structural class (same alpha, same deg) at different numerical precision; here both the structural class AND the functional form differ. The 'restriction' framing is a parametrization-of-domain statement, orthogonal to the (iv) independence determination.
